name: Wetwall Night Crawler's Stealth Wrap
description: Everything about this outfit is built around moving through the Shelf after dark without being seen, heard, or remembered. The foundation is a skin-close base layer in dark navy, barely distinguishable from black, in a moisture-wicking weave that's been hand-dyed unevenly — the dye job is amateur but effective, breaking up any reflective sheen. Over that: a long-sleeved pullover in matte dark gray, the neck cut low and wide enough to pull up over the nose, the cuffs long enough to cover the wrists entirely. The outer layer is a deconstructed hooded jacket, its original shape somewhere between a coach's shell and a rain anorak, now cut down, re-seamed, and fitted with a series of interior pockets accessible through hidden slits — one at the chest, two at the lower hem, one inside each sleeve near the wrist. The hood is deep and can be cinched to a narrow oval around the face. The whole jacket is treated with a matte-finish waterproofing compound that kills any surface sheen. Trousers are slim-fit in heavy black cotton twill, the inner ankle seams reinforced with self-repair tape to prevent snagging. Boots are soft-soled, mid-ankle, in worn synthetic suede that's been re-dyed black — near-silent on most Shelf flooring, with a thin but grippy rubber sole. Thin knit gloves in charcoal complete the set. There is nothing reflective anywhere on this outfit. No hardware, no exposed metal, no pale thread.
functionality: Full matte treatment eliminates reflective signature in low-light environments. Deep hood and face-covering collar allow near-complete concealment without additional gear. Hidden interior pocket system distributes carried items close to the body, reducing profile and sound. Soft-soled boots minimize footfall noise. Moisture-wicking base layer manages heat during sustained movement.
what_it_says: This person does not want to be seen. Whether that's survival pragmatism, profession, or necessity is left entirely open — but the level of deliberate care in eliminating every reflective surface says this is not accidental. They move at night, they move quietly, and they've thought about it.
worn_by: anyone who survives by being overlooked
manufacturer: Jacket is heavily modified from a PolyRoute surplus shell; remaining pieces are Shelf market finds, hand-dyed and self-treated
story_hooks: The hidden wrist-sleeve pocket contains something the wearer was paid to deliver three days ago and hasn't been able to — the recipient has gone dark and the client is getting impatient.
A Tier 2 CorpSec surveillance upgrade has added thermal imaging to the Shelf's eastern corridor — and this outfit, optimized for visible-light concealment, offers no protection against it.
Another night-runner recognizes the specific matte-treatment smell — it's a formula only one person on the Shelf makes, and that person disappeared two weeks ago.

physical_description.visual_profile: A ghost-like silhouette designed for nocturnal movement — layered in graduating darks from navy to charcoal to black, with intentional irregularity in the dye work that breaks up any readable shape. The overall impression is of controlled shapelessness: a figure built to blend into shadows rather than stand out.
physical_description.fit: Skin-close base layer; relaxed pullover over it; deconstructed jacket fitted but not tailored, allowing freedom of movement. Trousers slim but not restrictive. Every piece coordinates for silent, unobstructed motion — no excess fabric to snag or rustle.
physical_description.primary_material: Navy moisture-wicking synthetic blend (base); dark gray matte jersey (pullover); heavily treated PolyRoute surplus shell (jacket, now deconstructed); heavy black cotton twill (trousers); worn synthetic suede (boots); charcoal knit (gloves)
physical_description.texture: Dull throughout — matte-finish waterproofing on jacket kills sheen; hand-dyed base layer shows irregular pooling and fading; worn suede on boots is soft and absorptive; knit gloves have subtle nap. Nothing catches light. Everything feels broken-in or deliberately aged.
physical_description.color_scheme: Navy-to-charcoal-to-black gradient. No accents, no contrast. The unevenness of the hand-dye creates organic variation — darker patches, lighter zones — which serves the camouflage intent. Completely non-reflective.
physical_description.closures: Jacket: no visible zippers or snaps — hidden slit closures for interior pockets. Hood: friction-fit cinch cord (likely dark paracord or treated synthetic). Pullover: pullover neck. Trousers: likely friction-fit or internal elastic (no visible hardware). Boots: soft-sided, probably pull-on or hidden lacing.
distinctive_features: Deep hood cinchable to narrow oval — covers most of face
Hidden slit pockets: chest (1), lower hem (2), inside each sleeve near wrist (2) — no visible hardware
Hand-dyed base layer with intentional unevenness — breaks reflectivity and readability
Deconstructed jacket — original seams unpicked, re-fitted, excess removed
Reinforced inner ankle seams on trousers with self-repair tape
Matte-finish waterproofing treatment on entire outer layer
Soft-soled boots with grippy thin rubber — near-silent on Shelf flooring
Zero reflective elements — no zippers, no metal hardware, no pale thread
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4–5 (working class/sub-grade). This is not expensive gear — it's built from surplus and shelf-market finds, hand-modified. The sophistication is in intent and execution, not materials cost.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street operative, scavenger, or covert nighttime worker. Someone who needs to move through the Shelf (ungoverned sectors, likely flooded or industrial ruins) undetected. Not corporate (no branding, no polish). Not military (too improvised). This outfit speaks to self-reliance, illicit movement, and knowledge of low-visibility ops.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn but maintained. The hand-dye unevenness and worn suede are intentional — breaking reflectivity is the goal. Trousers show reinforced ankle tape. Nothing pristine, nothing flashy. Gear that's been used and will be used again.

image_prompt: A lean figure in a cyberpunk Shelf district, dressed head-to-toe in matte dark navy-to-black layers, photographed at dusk in deep shadow. The deconstructed jacket hangs loose and shapeless; the deep hood is cinched tight, obscuring most of the face, leaving only the lower jaw and chin visible. One gloved hand pulls the hood tighter. Behind: crumbling concrete infrastructure, dim industrial lighting, pools of standing water reflecting no detail. The figure is nearly monochromatic — the eye struggles to find a clean outline. Moody, low-key lighting; cool color grading. Shot from slight distance to show the full ghostlike silhouette. No reflections, no highlights on fabric. --ar 2:3 --v 6
